root_cause.text: In the `e1000_tx_map` function, an unnecessary decrement of the `count` variable in the DMA error cleanup path causes an off-by-one error that prevents one successfully mapped TX buffer from being unmapped when a subsequent mapping operation fails.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (count) count--;` block immediately preceding the `while (count--)` loop in both `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c` and `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000e/netdev.c`, which aligns with the CVE description stating that "Decrementing count before the while loop in dma_error causes an off-by-one error" and results in "exactly one DMA mapping [leaking]" if any prior mapping was successful.

vuln_statements.explanation: This while loop in the DMA error cleanup path decrements count during iteration. Due to the off-by-one error where count was prematurely decremented elsewhere before reaching this cleanup handler, one successfully mapped TX buffer will not be unmapped, causing a resource leak.

Same vulnerability pattern in e1000e driver variant. The while(count--) loop in dma_error label attempts to unmap previously successful TX buffers, but the premature count decrement causes one buffer to remain unmapped.
